justification: Changes which council rules the nightly quote check may mark proven from picture OCR, and proven rules are served as the council's own words. No schema change; the change lands at the next council_quote run.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: glued OCR text proves a rule with an added space inside a word ('no tin' for 'not in'), a rule word cut out of a longer OCR word, a changed number, or '12' for '1/2'; or a spaceless OCR line of the real rule is not proven
falsifiable_check.observed_red: On origin/main test_ocr_that_dropped_the_spaces_still_proves_the_rule fails (prove returns None). Hornsby residential dry run (chapter_314.json, cached PDF): before 0 of 67 picture rules proven, after 32 of 67; text-layer rules proven on picture pages 0 of 808.

pre_impl.existing_data: Hornsby part 3 residential dry run 2026-10-27: 147 not_found. 80 were reader inventions from the contents page (page 2), 67 sat on precinct diagram pages where RapidOCR returns text with spaces dropped.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The matcher assumed OCR keeps word spaces. RapidOCR merges whole lines into one token on these diagrams.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds one helper used as a second test inside the existing prove(); the original exact-order match is unchanged and runs first.

functions.name: _glued_match
functions.input: the normalised rule text and the normalised OCR text of one picture
functions.output: True when the rule tokens appear in order with OCR spaces possibly missing, no OCR space inside a rule token, and the stretch starts and ends on OCR token edges
functions.if_none: empty rule text returns False, so nothing is proven

functions.name: prove
functions.input: rule body, PDF path, stored page number, optional OCR function
functions.output: quote and quote_page when the rule is printed in one picture on the page or either side
functions.if_none: returns None and the rule stays unconfirmed and hidden

values.if_missing: no picture or no OCR engine gives None, so the rule stays unconfirmed

break_it.scenario: Glued OCR joins two words so a different rule reads the same letters ('no tin' / 'not in').
break_it.what_happens: A rule would be served as council words that the council did not print.
break_it.how: Any OCR space inside the matched stretch must fall on a rule word boundary; test_a_space_added_inside_a_rule_word_is_still_not_proven.

break_it.scenario: The rule's first word is the tail of a longer OCR word ('Noparking...' proving 'parking...').
break_it.what_happens: A negation dropped from the start would flip the meaning of a served rule.
break_it.how: The stretch must start and end on OCR token edges; test_glued_text_must_not_cut_a_rule_word_out_of_a_longer_word.

break_it.scenario: Text-layer rules of the chapter get proven by chance against diagram OCR.
break_it.what_happens: Rules would be proven on the wrong page with a wrong page link.
break_it.how: Measured on Hornsby residential: 0 of 808 text-layer rules proven on any picture page.
break_it.repro: dry run script: prove(rule, cached Hornsby PDF, page) for every text-layer rule and every picture page

post_merge.db_reset: No. Takes effect at the next council_quote run; nothing is written by this PR.
